chunks.arabic_text: ١ - وَهَبُ بْنُ وَهْبٍ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زَمَعَةَ بْنِ الْأَسْوَدِ بْنِ الْمُطَّلِبِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعُزَّى، أَبُو الْبَخْتَرِيِّ، الْقَاضِي.

translations.en: 1 – Wahb ibn Wahb ibn Abdullah ibn Zama'a ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abd al-Uzza, Abu al-Bakhtari, the judge.

chunks.arabic_text: كَذَّابٌ، عَامِيّ، إِلَّا أَنْ لَهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) أَحَادِيثَ كُلُّهَا لَا يُوثَقُ بِهَا.

translations.en: A liar, an ʿāmī (commoner/non-specialist), except that he has hadith from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), all of which are not to be relied upon.

en.summary: Wahb ibn Wahb, a descendant of the Quraysh clan of Banu Zama'a, is characterized in al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* as a 'liar' and an 'ʿāmī' (non-specialist in hadith sciences), highlighting the tension between noble lineage and scholarly rigor in Shia biographical evaluation. Despite transmitting from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), his narrations are deemed unreliable (*la yuthiq bihi*) for deriving legal rulings, illustrating the critical Shia methodology of prioritizing precision in transmission over mere proximity to the Imams.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Wahb ibn Wahb as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.كَذَّابٌ: Liar (a specific grade of weakness in narrators)
key_terms.لَا يُوثَقُ بِهَا: Not to be relied upon / Weak (indicating the narrations are not trustworthy)
